title: Windows service installation from a public or temporary path
description: Detects a new Windows service whose image path points into a public-user or temporary directory and therefore warrants investigation.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may install a Windows service to establish execution or persistence.
hypothesis.rationale: Service creation is legitimate administration but can also provide durable privileged execution when its binary path or creator is unusual.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify service-install events that execute from selected public-user or temporary paths while leaving normal service paths unmatched.

triage.summary: Review the service path, creating context, host role, and surrounding process activity before escalation.
steps: Confirm whether the service and installation source are approved for the affected host.
Inspect the service image path, signer, parent activity, account, and adjacent process events.
Escalate unexpected privileged services or suspicious paths for host investigation.
false_positives: Approved software installation or endpoint-management activity that stages a service binary in a temporary directory

validation.expected_outcome: Match Service Control Manager event 7045 when ImagePath contains a selected public-user or temporary path; do not match other event identifiers, providers, or normal service paths.
